findings.title: Repeated USE failures drain connection pool permanently, unlike base's warn+keep
findings.claim: A keyspace whose USE keeps failing empties the node's connection pool for good, since PoolRefiller::current_keyspace is stored before USE succeeds and is never cleared on failure, so every refill retries the same failing USE and each new connection is discarded while had_error_since_last_refill triggers a backoff-scheduled refill that repeats the failure as existing connections die off unreplaced. The node ends up Broken(UseKeyspaceError) and a Lost event is sent, failing even fully-qualified queries to that node. In the base, the same failure was logged with warn! and the connection was still returned Ok, so the node stayed usable.

findings.title: USE failure log downgraded from warn! to debug!, hiding pool drain
findings.claim: The head downgrades the USE failure log from warn! (base) to debug!, so operators see nothing at default verbosity while the pool drains, only noticing once the node is already Broken. The sibling 'Failed to change keyspace' log still uses warn!.

findings.title: UseKeyspaceError mapped to ConnectionError misclassifies server rejections as faults
findings.claim: ConnectionError is meant for connections that can no longer be used, but the only producer maps every UseKeyspaceError into it, including a server rejecting USE over an otherwise-healthy connection, KeyspaceNameMismatch, and timeouts. In each case the pool becomes Broken and the node is reported Lost over what may be a keyspace problem, and the error text omits the keyspace name.

findings.title: keyspace_setup_failure_triggers_refill never drives a refill or backoff
findings.claim: keyspace_setup_failure_triggers_refill is a sync test on an empty pool where need_filling() is already true before the event, and run() is never driven, so no refill or backoff is ever actually observed. It also builds an event impossible in production (requested_shard: Some with keyspace_name: None, when the real producer always sets keyspace_name: Some) and bumps the gauge by hand instead of using the real open path.

findings.title: keyspace_setup_failure_preserves_pool_state has unbounded waits and skippable cleanup
findings.claim: keyspace_setup_failure_preserves_pool_state has two ready_connections.next().await waits with no timeout, so a misbehaving proxy would hang the test, and proxy.finish() never runs if an assertion fails, leaving cleanup skipped. It also never asserts had_error_since_last_refill, doesn't cover a shard-aware (requested_shard: Some) attempt, and increments the gauge by hand.

findings.title: Metric tests don't exercise excess-connections term or real open/close paths
findings.claim: In the resharding test the excess list is empty, so the + excess_connections.len() term of the decrement is never exercised. All metric tests increment the gauge by hand rather than through real flows, and in full_pool_* a 5s timeout bounds the poll such that if it fires the spawned worker and proxy are never cleaned up.

findings.title: Gauge leaks on shard-aware excess rejection and pool teardown (pre-existing)
findings.claim: A shard-aware connection rejected as excess is not decremented from the total_connections gauge, and pool teardown when run() exits doesn't decrement remaining connections either. The full_pool_* test's final assertion (get_total_connections() == 1 after the worker exits) locks this leak in; this is pre-existing and not caused by this PR.

findings.title: decrement_total_connections loops instead of using a single atomic subtract
findings.claim: decrement_total_connections calls dec_total_connections() once per connection in a loop; a single dec_total_connections_by(n) would do the same subtract atomically.

findings.title: Test uses 1ms busy-poll instead of Notify or paused time
findings.claim: The 1ms poll in the test could be replaced with a Notify or with paused time instead of busy-polling.

findings.title: Clear sites must remember to call decrement_total_connections manually
findings.claim: The per-connection decrement loop is redundant work, and every conns.clear() / excess_connections.clear() site must remember to call decrement_total_connections first; a future clear site that forgets would inflate total_connections.

findings.title: Metric decrement split by error kind creates branch-coupling risk
findings.claim: Only the Keyspace branch decrements the metric, because the increment happens at open time; both branches repeat the !self.is_filling() && self.is_empty() check, so moving the increment would require editing both together.

findings.title: ConnectionSetupError lacks Debug derive and is confusable with similar name
findings.claim: ConnectionSetupError has no #[derive(Debug)], which is why tests hand-match it with panic! instead of using standard assertions. Its name is also very close to the public ConnectionSetupRequestError.

findings.title: unrequested_connection_event helper name is undocumented and unclear
findings.claim: unrequested_connection_event (meaning 'no requested shard') has no doc comment and nearly duplicates shard_aware_attempt_result.

findings.title: Keyspace tests duplicate scaffolding instead of reusing test helpers
findings.claim: The keyspace tests build PoolRefiller::new(..) by hand instead of using mock_pool_refiller(), hand-encode the SetKeyspace response with no comment, and duplicate start_simulated_node.

findings.title: All four commits lack bodies, hiding several bundled changes
findings.claim: All four commits in the PR have no commit body. 7f48315d's subject also hides several bundled changes: moving the keyspace check ahead of resharding, the new public ConnectionError::UseKeyspaceError variant, the warn! to debug! log-level change, and the new backoff flag plus metric decrement.

findings.title: Fix and test split across commits with an unsquashed fixup commit
findings.claim: de164845 changes metric accounting with no accompanying test, and the tests only arrive later in 0d91aa54. 617139df only changes that test's wait and should be squashed into it rather than left as a separate fixup.

findings.title: PR body omits metrics fix/tests and references an unresolvable issue
findings.claim: The PR body only describes 7f48315d and doesn't mention the metrics fix or its tests. The stated 'Fixes: #1682' doesn't resolve in this repository (gh issue view 1682 fails), and the validation filter keyspace_setup_failure only runs 2 tests; metrics is off by default so all #[cfg(feature = "metrics")] assertions and metric tests were never run.

findings.title: New tests skip calling setup_tracing() required by CONTRIBUTING
findings.claim: The two new tests skip calling setup_tracing(), even though CONTRIBUTING asks new tests to call it and every other test in the module does.

findings.title: New error message breaks existing UseKeyspaceError formatting pattern
findings.claim: The new error message breaks the module's existing pattern: neighbouring setup variants use #[error(transparent)], and every other UseKeyspaceError wrapper uses the "'USE KEYSPACE <>' request failed: {0}" format, but this one follows neither convention.

findings.title: Undocumented reordering: keyspace check now blocks resharding, causing stale sharder
findings.claim: Moving the keyspace check ahead of resharding changes completion ordering without documentation: in the base, maybe_reshard, the shard-aware-port update, and the mismatch check all ran before USE, but in the head they now wait on a USE round-trip that has no timeout. While USE keeps failing, the sharder and shard_aware_port stay stale so refills compute shard-aware ports from a stale sharder and port mismatches go undetected; if USE hangs, is_filling() stays true, suppressing refills so resharding never happens. The PR states 'completes keyspace setup before resharding' only as a test property, not as a described behaviour change.

findings.title: PR doesn't document log-level drop or new public error variant
findings.claim: The PR doesn't describe two observable behaviour changes: the log-level drop from warn! to debug!, and the new public ConnectionError variant now surfaced through ConnectionPoolError::Broken. The variant itself does have a doc comment, so that part of the review checklist holds.
